correctness.rationale: For cycle partition λ of M, sampling a uniformly random point weights a part of size j by j/M, hence μ=S2/M and E[P²]=S3/M; at fixed M equality of μ and variance is equivalent to matching integer (S2,S3). A partition-generating recurrence C_k(m,s,t)=C_(k-1)(m,s,t)+C_k(m-k,s-k²,t-k³) is exhaustive by the include/exclude-one-k argument. Independently generated every integer partition at M=1..14 and recomputed power-sum fibers without using source recurrence: none collide below 14, and at 14 the unique double-fiber (74,434) consists exactly of (7,4,3) and (6,6,1,1). Explicit sums verify μ=37/7 and v=150/49. Adding M-14 1-cycles increases both power sums by M-14, producing an algebraically proved witness for every larger M. The cutoff is exhaustive for a finite interval, not a claimed exhaustive classification above 14.

value.rationale: Identifiability of cycle structure from low-order orbit statistics is a natural inverse-dynamical question. The first failure threshold at 14, uniqueness of the offending pair, and disjoint least-period supports give an exact obstruction that future inverse problems can cite; the finite cutoff is motivated by distinguishability, not an arbitrary sample of partitions.

final_claim: At each cardinality M<=13 the uniform-point least-period mean and variance uniquely determine a permutation cycle type. At M=14 there is exactly one nontrivial collision, partitions (7,4,3) versus (6,6,1,1), with (S2,S3)=(74,434), mean 37/7 and variance 150/49. The pair remains nonidentifying for every M>=14 by appending fixed points.
